issues.description: Test inputs now smuggle a zero-amount, zero-puzzle-hash addition where the previous test passed [], silently mutating the postcondition.
issues.detail: Tests changed `additions=[]` to `additions=[Addition(amount=uint64(0), puzzle_hash=bytes32.zeros)]`. The precondition of `cat_spend` is undocumented here, but a zero-amount addition to the zero puzzle hash is not equivalent to no additions. Either the new path requires a phantom addition (a defect) or the test no longer exercises the original case. Both are unreasoned.

issues.description: `send_transaction` silently drops the `puzzle_decorator[0]`-only slicing semantics it previously guaranteed.
issues.detail: The original code passed `[request.puzzle_decorator[0].to_json_dict()]` — exactly one decorator. The new path forwards `request.puzzle_decorator` whole to `CreateSignedTransaction.puzzle_decorator`, then `_generate_signed_transaction` iterates all of them. The postcondition has changed without any stated specification of which is correct. Unreasoned change of observable behavior.

issues.description: `cat_discrepancy_validation` uses `None in {extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution}` — a set whose membership check depends on hashability and equality of `bytes` and `str`.
issues.detail: The expression relies on set construction with mixed types and `None` membership semantics. It happens to work, but it is opaque and fragile: a reader cannot state the invariant without simulating Python's hashing. A clear `any(x is None for x in (...))` would make the disjunction explicit. Style is substance when correctness must be read off the page.

issues.description: `get_wallet(...)` is called purely for its side effect of raising — labelled by a comment, not by structure.
issues.detail: The pattern `# opportunity to raise` followed by a discarded call is a smuggled assertion. The precondition (wallet exists and has the required type) is now enforced by an unnamed side effect whose return value is thrown away. A named guard — `self._assert_wallet_exists(...)` — would make the contract explicit instead of folkloric.

issues.description: `cat_spend` no longer enforces the per-addition `MAX_COIN_AMOUNT` check that the old code stated explicitly.
issues.detail: The removed branch raised `ValueError(f"Coin amount cannot exceed {MAX_COIN_AMOUNT}")` per addition. The new path assumes `create_signed_transaction` enforces the same postcondition. If it does, the check is redundant and should be removed deliberately with a citation; if it does not, a precondition has been silently dropped. No reasoning is offered either way.

issues.description: Three `# type: ignore[arg-type]` suppressions are duplicated by extraction rather than eliminated.
issues.detail: The comment "Curious that mypy doesn't see the elif" is now copied into a free function where the same narrowing failure persists. A `TypeGuard` or an early-return restructuring would prove to the type checker — and the reader — that the three values are non-None. Extracting code without strengthening its specification is mere motion.

review.summary: REASONED in intent, UNREASONED in execution. The deduplication is the right direction, but the diff repeatedly substitutes "we'll route it through the other endpoint" for stated pre/postconditions. Two behavioral changes are silent: `puzzle_decorator` is no longer sliced to its first element in `send_transaction`, and the per-addition `MAX_COIN_AMOUNT` check in `cat_spend` is removed without justification. The test diff that replaces `additions=[]` with a zero-amount, zero-puzzle-hash addition is the loudest tell: the old postcondition was not preserved, so the test was edited to fit the new code rather than the new code edited to fit the spec. DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE: `get_wallet` is called purely to raise, annotated only by a comment. TESTED-NOT-PROVED throughout. Refusal would be inappropriate — the refactor is valuable — but the author must state the equivalence claim explicitly before merge.
